writing.task1: The line graph illustrates how the prices of three metals, namely copper, nickel and zinc, changed on average each month during 2014. Overall, the prices of all three metals fluctuated considerably over the year, and nickel showed the most dramatic changes, while copper was the most stable. At the beginning of the year, nickel prices rose sharply and reached a peak in around May, with an increase of roughly ten percent. After that, however, the price of nickel fell significantly and it continued to drop for most of the second half of the year. Zinc prices followed a different pattern. They increased moderately in the first half of the year, then decreased in the summer before recovering slightly towards December. Copper prices, in contrast, changed only a little from month to month. They fell slightly at the start of the year, remained fairly flat in the middle months and declined again near the end of 2014. In summary, nickel was the most volatile metal, whereas copper showed the smallest monthly changes.
writing.task2: In many parts of the world, people are living much longer than in the past because of better healthcare and living conditions. While some believe that an ageing population causes serious problems for governments, others argue that it brings benefits to society. In my opinion, although there are some advantages, the disadvantages are more significant. On the one hand, older people can contribute a lot to society. Many retired people have valuable experience and skills, and they often work as volunteers or help their families by looking after grandchildren. This allows younger parents to work full time, which supports the economy. In addition, older people spend money on travel and services, which creates jobs in these industries. On the other hand, an ageing population creates heavy financial pressure on governments. As the number of retired people increases, governments must spend more on pensions and healthcare, while the number of young workers who pay taxes becomes smaller. For example, in some European countries and in Japan, the cost of looking after elderly citizens has already become a major burden on the national budget. Furthermore, hospitals and care homes may not have enough staff to meet the growing demand, which can reduce the quality of care for everyone. In conclusion, while elderly people can make useful contributions to their families and communities, I believe the economic and social problems caused by an ageing population outweigh the benefits. Governments should therefore plan ahead, for instance by encouraging people to work longer and by investing in healthcare systems.

I would like to talk about my friend Rafi, whom I met about four years ago when I started my first year at college in Dhaka. We were sitting next to each other in a chemistry class, and we started talking because neither of us understood the teacher's explanation. At first I thought he was quite quiet and serious, but later I realised he has a great sense of humour. After class we went to the canteen together and found out that we both liked cricket and the same films. Since then we have studied together for almost every exam, and we often play cricket on Fridays. I think we became good friends because we support each other. When I had problems with my studies, he helped me, and when his family moved to a new area, I helped him to settle in. We also trust each other and can talk about anything.

I think it is quite important for children to have friends at school, but they don't need a lot of friends. Having two or three close friends can help them feel happy and confident, and they learn how to share and cooperate with other people.
